highlight.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows Go Live
highlight.summary: <cite index="15-1,15-4">GitHub Agentic Workflows let you automate repository tasks using AI agents that run within GitHub Actions, with workflows written in plain Markdown instead of complex YAML for intelligent decision-making in issue triage, pull request reviews, and CI failure analysis.</cite> <cite index="15-8,15-10">The feature is available through the gh aw CLI extension, allowing teams to describe automation goals in natural language and let AI agents figure out implementation.</cite>

resources.title: Claude Code Dominates CLI Agent Wars
resources.why_now: <cite index="4-14,4-15">Claude Code is the undisputed king of CLI-based agentic coding with Opus 4.6 handling complex multi-file tasks, test generation, and repository-wide refactors better than anything else on the market.</cite> <cite index="4-4">If the trend continues, Codex could pull even with Claude Code by mid-2026, making this a critical time to evaluate terminal-based AI tools.</cite>

resources.title: Modern CLI Tools Renaissance Continues
resources.why_now: <cite index="3-8,3-9">If you install one tool from this list, make it fzf - it's a general-purpose fuzzy finder that plugs into everything: shell history search, file navigation, git branch switching, even Kubernetes pod selection.</cite> <cite index="5-5,5-6">The command line has quietly entered its renaissance with new tools that are faster, more beautiful, and surprisingly fun to use.</cite>

resources.title: Cursor vs VS Code: The AI-Native Editor Battle
resources.why_now: <cite index="24-17">The shift toward agent-based coding workflows in early 2026, where the editor itself executes multi-step refactors and runs tests autonomously, has made AI-native editors hard to beat for any team that ships frequently.</cite> <cite index="24-14,24-15">At MG Software we use Cursor as our primary code editor due to its deep AI integration that significantly increases development speed while maintaining compatibility with VS Code extensions.</cite>

resources.title: GitHub Actions Gets Security-First Overhaul
resources.why_now: <cite index="14-17,14-18">The 2026 GitHub Actions roadmap responds directly to supply chain attacks by shifting the platform toward secure-by-default, verifiable automation with a focus on disrupting these attacks.</cite> <cite index="14-5,14-6">These protections scale across repositories without per-workflow configuration, with enterprises applying consistent policies organization-wide using rulesets and repository custom properties.</cite>

claude_take: The developer tooling landscape is consolidating around AI-first experiences, with terminal-native agents like Claude Code and AI-integrated editors like Cursor fundamentally changing how we write code. GitHub's move to natural language workflow definitions signals that even infrastructure automation is becoming more accessible, while the CLI renaissance proves that performance and user experience improvements still matter in our foundational tools.
